english: Tuition goes up every year.
tip: 마다 (mada = every) follows a noun: 해마다 (haemada = every year).

english: I really want to get a scholarship.
tip: -고 싶다 = 'want to': 받고 싶어요 (batgo sipeoyo = want to receive).

english: I got a scholarship this time, so I'm really glad.
tip: -아서/어서 links cause and result: 받아서 기뻐요 (badaseo gippeoyo = got it, so glad).

english: My sibling got a scholarship and is very happy.
tip: 3rd-person feelings take -어해요: 기뻐해요 (gippeohaeyo = is glad), not 기뻐요.

english: The senior treats the juniors to a meal.
tip: 한테 (hante) marks the receiver: 후배들한테 (hubaedeulhante = to the juniors).

english: The club meeting is on Friday evening.
tip: 에 (e) marks a time: 저녁에 (jeonyeoge = in the evening).

english: I joined the photography club.
tip: 가입하다 (gaipada = to join) takes 에: 동아리에 가입해요 (dongarie gaipaeyo).

english: I'm going to Japan as an exchange student.
tip: (으)로 marks a role: 교환 학생으로 (gyohwan haksaengeuro = as an exchange student).

english: Next year I'm going to study abroad in the US.
tip: 유학을 가요 (yuhageul gayo) marks study-abroad with object 을 (eul) – not the destination -에 (-e) you'd expect with 'go'. Study-abroad is what you go, not where.

english: I need a foreign-language test score.
tip: 필요하다 (piryohada = to need) takes 이/가: 점수가 필요해요 (jeomsuga piryohaeyo).

english: Now I've gotten used to local life a lot.
tip: -아/어지다 = 'become': 익숙해졌어요 (iksukhaejyeosseoyo = got used to).

english: My homestay family is really kind.
tip: For elders, use honorific -세요: 친절하세요 (chinjeolhaseyo = is kind).

target: 저는 여름 방학에 배낭여행을 갈 거예요.
english: I'll go backpacking this summer vacation.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 = 'will': 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo = will go).

english: Colleges are decided by the exam score.
tip: (으)로 marks the means: 점수로 (jeomsuro = by the score).

english: I couldn't solve a single math problem.
tip: 하나도 + 못 = 'not a single one': 하나도 못 풀었어요 (hanado mot pureosseoyo).

english: After the exam I felt really relieved.
tip: -고 = 'and then': 끝나고 (kkeunnago = it ends, and then).

english: My sibling is stressed because of the exam.
tip: 때문에 (ttaemune = because of) follows a noun: 수능 때문에 (suneung ttaemune).

english: I send my child to piano academy.
tip: 에 marks the destination: 학원에 보내요 (hagwone bonaeyo = send to the academy).

english: The academy fees are pricier than I thought.
tip: 보다 (boda = than) marks comparison: 생각보다 (saenggakboda = than I thought).

target: 동생이 이번 시험을 아주 잘 봤어요.
english: My sibling did really well on this exam.
tip: Korean sees a test: 보다 (boda) 'to see' is the take-an-exam verb – 시험을 봤어요 (siheomeul bwasseoyo) = took (saw) the exam.

english: I showed my report card to my parents.
tip: Respect runs through the whole phrase: 부모님께 (bumonimkke) uses honorific 'to', and 보여 드렸어요 (boyeo deuryeosseoyo) uses humble 드리다 (deurida) 'give' – showing done upward.

english: I studied hard and passed the exam.
tip: 시험에 붙었어요 (siheome buteosseoyo) – note the 에 (e): you stick TO the exam, so passing takes the 'to' particle, not an object marker.

english: This time I'll definitely pass, I promise.
tip: 합격할게요 (hapgyeokhalgeyo) ends in -(으)ㄹ게요 (-(eu)lgeyo), a promise made TO your listener – plain future -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (-(eu)l geoyeyo) would just predict, not commit.

english: The teacher announced the exam results.
tip: honorific past -셨어요: 발표하셨어요 (balpyohasyeosseoyo = announced).

english: I applied for the Korean proficiency test.
tip: 신청하다 (sincheonghada = to apply) takes 을/를: 시험을 신청해요 (siheomeul sincheonghaeyo).

english: The report is due tomorrow.
tip: 까지 (kkaji = until) marks a limit: 내일까지 (naeilkkaji = until tomorrow).

english: I was so nervous when presenting.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 발표할 때 (balpyohal ttae = when presenting).

target: 매일 새 단어를 열 개씩 외워요.
english: I memorize ten new words each day.
tip: -씩 (-ssik) means 'each/apiece': 열 개씩 (yeol gaessik = ten each).

english: For problems I don't know, I ask the teacher.
tip: 께 marks the honored receiver: 선생님께 (seonsaengnimkke = to the teacher).

english: Grades come out as much as you put in.
tip: 만큼 (mankeum = as much as) follows a word: 노력한 만큼 (noryeokan mankeum = as much as you try).
